draft_memo.title: CareBridge Remote Consultations and Patient Satisfaction
draft_memo.body:
CareBridge's fictional patient survey recorded 80% satisfaction for remote consultations in 2025, compared with 78% in 2024 [P10]. CareBridge conducted 24,000 remote consultations in 2025, up from 20,000 in 2024 [P09]. Remote consultations represented 30% of its total consultations in 2025 [P09]. The surveys used different respondents each year [P10].

Interpretation: The data shows an increase in patient satisfaction alongside a rise in the number of remote consultations.

Limitations: The surveys used different respondents each year, which may limit the reliability of the satisfaction comparison. The data does not provide insights into the demographics of the respondents or the specific aspects of the consultations that contributed to satisfaction ratings. There is no information on the reasons behind the increase in remote consultations or satisfaction levels. The source does not detail the total number of consultations conducted in 2024, making it difficult to assess the overall growth in remote consultations. Additionally, the survey methodology is not described, leaving questions about its validity. The memo does not specify the geographic distribution of the respondents surveyed each year. There is no information on how patient satisfaction was measured or the survey questions used. The impact of external factors on patient satisfaction and consultation numbers is not addressed. The memo lacks comparative data from other healthcare providers for context on CareBridge's performance. The memo does not include any qualitative feedback from patients regarding their remote consultation experiences. There is no analysis of how patient satisfaction may vary across different types of consultations. The impact of technological issues on patient satisfaction during remote consultations is not discussed. No longitudinal data is provided to assess trends in patient satisfaction over multiple years.
